kiln_p06_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_001.text: Su Yan arrived before the hall's first ordinary shift, wearing a travel coat dusted with road frost. Yue recognised her from the way she paused at the gate to read the actual notice before accepting anyone's summary. The examiner greeted Luo, then asked where an arriving visitor should leave muddy boots. Nothing in her ninth-stage cultivation made mud useful inside a calibrated room. Han brought a brush and looked delighted to provide a task for such an important pair of feet. Yue felt some of her anxious awe turn into a memory of an ordinary teacher.

kiln_p06_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_002.text: Peng showed the examiner the paid placement, recent work roster and current clinic record. Yue waited beside the comparison-room door, resisting the urge to explain every favorable result aloud. Su Yan read the sleep disruption as carefully as the improved reserve. She asked who would supervise practice between visits and who could halt it when ordinary recovery changed. Luo named the clinic examiner for the physical checks and himself for the permitted room sessions, subject to a reviewed method. Su Yan asked about his training qualification before asking about his schedule. Good intentions would not certify a route.

kiln_p06_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_003.text: Luo's relevant certificate covered supervised primary-route practice within the local Azure Cloud programme, with no authority to certify Yue's next stage alone. He had not used its lower-limb teaching section recently and would review it before taking that task. The clinic examiner had agreed to provide independent ordinary recovery checks, not meridian instruction. Su Yan could visit on her circuit and perform formal assessment with another qualified examiner later. The arrangement was possible, not yet complete. Yue found the precision reassuring until Su Yan asked how much actual time Luo could offer without abandoning live kiln duties.

kiln_p06_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_004.text: Luo counted two short room sessions per ordinary work week, with any live firing responsibility taking priority before a session began. Those sessions would not be interrupted midway for convenient kiln errands. Peng could reserve the room times and assign an ordinary replacement at the archive bench. Yue would receive her wage for the agreed work arrangement; training provision had to be separately funded before new practice. The owner joined the discussion and asked for a real finite estimate. Yue expected to be embarrassed by the cost. Instead she was relieved to hear it spoken before she owed anything.

kiln_p06_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_005.text: Su Yan inspected the comparison room while it was cold and empty. The replacement lead had its current rating; the reference seal showed when the panel had been opened. She asked Yue to identify the blank reference and grounding exit without looking at the labels. Yue did. Then Su Yan switched two ordinary uncharged instruments and asked again. Yue caught the change but hesitated. The teacher smiled at the hesitation rather than demand immediate confidence. Knowing when to inspect was more valuable than performing familiarity for someone who had already seen her make mistakes.

kiln_p06_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_006.text: The first reference comparison produced an odd warmth at the copper contact. Yue had not admitted any trace. Su Yan removed the thread, checked the blank and found that a warming brick stood too near the table beneath the cover. Someone had moved it there to make the room pleasant for the visiting examiner. Luo remembered authorising warmth without specifying the position. The brick went to an ordinary safe corner. They waited for the bench to settle and repeated the blank checks. The room could be comfortable only after comfort stopped impersonating a spiritual result.

kiln_p06_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_007.text: Yue blushed because she had secretly enjoyed the warm contact. It made the instruments seem ready to welcome a stronger reading. Su Yan asked her to record the false comparison in her own study history. The lesson would otherwise belong only to a story about somebody else's brick. Yue wrote the actual condition and the corrected blank. She had not failed a stage or suffered a route injury. She had found an environmental error before practice, which was exactly what the cold check existed to do. Embarrassment could become useful without needing to become catastrophe.

kiln_p06_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_008.text: After the ordinary room checks, Su Yan heard the cup trial account. She inspected the guarded failed specimen and its linked release note rather than warming it with her own qi. A higher-stage examiner could overwhelm a modest vessel by doing the wrong helpful thing. The association specialist arrived with the instructor before noon and set up the funded grounded comparison. Yue remained a disconnected observer. Su Yan reviewed the plan but did not replace the specialist's method. Each person's qualification belonged to a defined question, not to a general right to make every important object behave.

kiln_p06_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_009.text: The four candidate cups entered the guarded modest-load evaluation individually, with separate release and cold inspection between them. Three matched the permitted reference behavior within the tested method. One held residual surface warmth beyond the accepted comparison at the handle join and was retired from teaching use. The result covered three specific revised cups, under that bench and load. It did not certify every future vessel. Tan copied the identities and allowed conditions correctly. Zhu looked satisfied rather than triumphant. A partial useful result could justify a next step without turning an unfinished process into a miracle.

kiln_p06_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_010.text: The retired fourth cup had a slightly altered lower handle join, visible in the forming record. Zhu had corrected its shape late in the wet stage. The specialist could not prove that correction alone caused the release difference, but the association's defined tolerance did not include the resulting geometry. Zhu would keep future retained trial pieces within the tested profile or seek a separately funded variation. Yue asked how small a difference mattered. The specialist showed her the clearance that remained at the release lead. A small shape change could occupy a large portion of an already narrow margin.

kiln_p06_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_011.text: Su Yan asked Yue to compare the cup's lesson with her proposed next route. Yue first answered that one should stay within a rating. The teacher waited. Yue looked at the candidate set again. The three accepted cups had histories, not simply a shared appearance. Their future use depended on those actual conditions. A route's last recovered throughput mattered in the same way. Two people at the same stage could not borrow each other's safe input from a title. Su Yan nodded. She had wanted an explanation carried across changed material, not a sentence that sounded wise.

kiln_p06_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_012.text: At lunch, Han asked the examiner whether ninth-stage people needed ordinary soup. Su Yan said especially when cooks tried to test that question by withholding it. He gave her the largest bowl. She told a story about an expensive visitor who had mistaken a plain soup ladle for a ritual implement and offered to buy it. Luo said they should have sold him the whole kitchen. Peng asked who would replace the ladle. Yue listened to the familiar adults become a temporary silly household, and remembered that supervision could begin in trust without ceasing to require real checks.

kiln_p06_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_013.text: After lunch, Su Yan reviewed Yue's established fourth-stage performance at the settled bench. The reserve reading reflected the ordinary work and night's sleep actually completed, with sampling loss separated. It was better than the arrival baseline but below the proposed fifth-stage minimum. Compatibility was sound for current maintenance and still short of the new target. The two arm pairs completed their permitted brief tasks with independent interruption and full discharge. No leg trace was attempted. Su Yan wrote that today's results supported the current stage. A plan for more could begin without claiming more had already arrived.

kiln_p06_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_014.text: Yue expected a speech about patience. Su Yan asked what a working fifth stage would let her do that she could not reliably do now. Yue described separate support through established leg routes instead of depending only on an external conducting stitch from an arm pair. She wanted more controlled options in ordinary craft and rescue. She did not claim sustained talisman work, which belonged later. Su Yan asked whether those options would make bad lifting posture safe. Yue laughed before answering no. The teacher looked pleased. A useful ambition needed enough humor to survive its own grand phrasing.

kiln_p06_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_015.text: They spread the primary-route chart on the cold table. Its six inward and outward pairs included routes Yue had not opened. Her first two were the existing arm pairs. The proposed third pair followed a distinct anterior lower-limb path from foot through knee to the hip junction and return. The proposed fourth followed the posterior heel and calf path to that junction and return. The drawing did not open anything. Su Yan asked Yue to name which ordinary sensation could be mistaken for a trace at each point. The student found more possibilities than she enjoyed admitting.

kiln_p06_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_016.text: The two new pairs were not one route seen from opposite ends. Each had its own complementary inward and outward channel and would be taught, discharged and checked separately. They would not bridge extraordinary vessels or open the middle dantian. Yue traced the distinction on paper with an ordinary pencil. She had wanted a clear next step. The fifth stage contained two substantial new learning tasks, not a pleasing new name for the third pair alone. Su Yan said the local method would be agreed before any new admission so that desire could not quietly lower its standard later.

kiln_p06_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_017.text: Under that local Azure Cloud method, Yue would need at least thirty-six usable breath-units after ordinary work, sleep and the known sampling cost. Compatibility would need to reach at least ninety percent. Those figures were method thresholds, not a coin price for rank. Ordinary retained reserve could grow only within inspected capacity and recovered practice. No one would fill her lower dantian with borrowed workshop charge. Yue wrote the figures in the plan, feeling both the distance from her present reading and the relief of knowing what the future question actually asked.

kiln_p06_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_018.text: Each of the four primary pairs would perform a separate quarter-unit useful task. For a new leg pair, the planned brief delivery admitted half a unit over four ordinary breaths, with input no higher than an eighth-unit per breath or a lower recovered limit. Useful work did not equal admitted charge. They would ground the remaining charge, rest and check before switching. The apparatus for the leg task would be rated and cold-inspected before use. A larger reserve would not authorise a larger pulse. Yue copied that line twice because she knew which mistake she would most want to make.

kiln_p06_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_019.text: Formal fifth-stage assessment would require three independently calibrated trials on separate recovered days, with the permitted task order changed. An independent assessor would witness direction, commanded interruption and complete release through all four pairs, rather than take a teacher's confidence as proof. Ordinary next-day touch, grip and leg movement had to remain normal after each trial. A trial would wait if sleep, appetite, strain or injury changed the recovered condition. The successful moment would not become an earned stage until the final following-day review. Yue could hear how long the method would take even after the routes were ready.

kiln_p06_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_020.text: Su Yan asked her to explain why three recovered trials were not the same as three trials in one enthusiastic morning. Yue described accumulated pressure and the information only a following day could provide. She asked whether the new reserve minimum guaranteed no injury. It did not. Throughput, control, route condition and recovery remained separate. The teacher was glad she asked. A large number could otherwise become a superstition as powerful as an amulet. Yue looked at the chart's unopened paths and found them less glamorous after the plan, but more real. She wanted real more than she wanted glamorous.

kiln_p06_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_021.text: The owner priced an initial six-week supervised preparation block, including ordinary posture instruction, reference room upkeep, limited established-route maintenance and review time. It did not purchase a stage or require Yue to continue if the arrangement failed. A later new-route block would need review of ordinary recovery and a renewed finite allowance. Peng kept food and accommodation during authorised recovery in the agreed employment terms. Yue could leave with her earned wage and own notes, owing no training debt. The owner expected useful archive and craft work in return for the actual paid hours they had negotiated.

kiln_p06_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_022.text: Yue signed the plan after reading its withdrawal and renewal lines. She would begin with ordinary lower-limb alignment and a steadier retained reserve, not a new admission that afternoon. Luo would refresh his teaching section with Su Yan before supervising the relevant sessions. The clinic examiner would keep independent physical checks. Su Yan's circuit dates gave them real review points, with no promise to arrive instantly if weather closed the road. Yue felt the mixture of warmth and limitation settle differently from disappointment. A teacher had made space for her without pretending the space had no walls.

kiln_p06_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_023.text: Luo spent the afternoon reviewing his own teaching under Su Yan's observation. Yue saw him miss a changed reference order and correct it before any live practice. He did not try to disguise the mistake in front of his student. Su Yan made him explain the ordinary leg posture and permitted discharge task on an uncharged model. Qualification did not make recent memory unnecessary. When the review ended, the next supervised preparation sessions were approved within the narrow agreed scope. The lower-limb route page remained unopened in Yue's body. It had become a plan others could actually help her follow.

kiln_p06_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_024.text: At the first ordinary posture lesson, Yue discovered that her right foot turned outward when she grew tired. The habit was subtle enough to hide while she concentrated. Luo had her walk a short ordinary path, then repeat after carrying an appropriate light basket with a partner. The outward turn returned. They stopped before pain and reduced the load. A future leg route would not straighten a joint by spiritual persuasion. Yue found the lesson less impressive than a new copper glow and more difficult than she had expected. Jian watched from the next bench and mercifully offered no title.

kiln_p06_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_025.text: Zhu did offer a title: Lady of the Wandering Toe. Yue threw a clean damp cloth at her and missed. Su Yan, passing the door, asked whether the cloth's flight had been assessed. Zhu said the method required three recovered attempts. The examiner laughed and ordered no actual repeat. Yue enjoyed the joke because the adults knew exactly which real standard they were parodying. They were not making bodily recovery optional. They were making it possible for a learner to remain human while following it. She picked up the cloth and finished the ordinary cleanup before supper.

kiln_p06_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_026.text: Su Yan stayed in the visitor room that night. Yue asked whether she regretted taking time from her circuit to see such modest progress. The teacher looked puzzled. New routes were substantial work for the body opening them; they did not need to entertain a ninth-stage observer. She had returned because Yue's questions had become worth supervising, and because the hall could supply a real arrangement. Yue felt unexpectedly close to tears. She had imagined earning attention by becoming stronger. Her teacher had noticed her becoming clearer about what strength could safely mean.

kiln_p06_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_027.text: They spoke of the ridge and earlier foundry only through records Yue actually owned. No optional branch object appeared on the table. Su Yan asked which earlier failure she still wanted to undo. Yue named more than one and then stopped. The teacher said a body could not train responsibly while every new task served as payment for an old helpless moment. Yue asked whether that meant letting go of caring. Su Yan shook her head. It meant choosing the present task by its present need, rather than asking it to rescue every past version of oneself.

kiln_p06_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_028.text: Upstairs, Yue tried to write that advice in an elegant sentence and failed. She settled for The next route is not an apology. Her roommate read the line while returning a borrowed pencil and asked who wanted one. Yue explained as much as she could without opening anybody else's record. The roommate said she had once repaired three customers' shoes badly because she wanted to make up for ruining the first pair. She had learned to charge properly for one sound repair. Yue stared, then laughed. Ordinary crafts had been teaching the same difficult lesson without a meridian chart.

kiln_p06_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_029.text: Su Yan left after the following morning's ordinary recovery check remained normal. Yue had performed only established-route tasks and posture work, so there was no new-pair result to carry into the departure. The teacher left the reviewed method, circuit dates and instructions for reducing practice if conditions changed. Her borrowed room key returned to the rack. Han gave her a little loaf, and she paid its ordinary price because the bakery had baked it. Yue watched her cross the yard with muddy boots already brushed. The coming months looked larger now, but less empty.

kiln_p06_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_030.text: The hall resumed its ordinary rhythm around the new preparation sessions. Yue found that progress began by repeating movements she could have mistaken for warmups beneath a grander lesson. A short aligned walk, a quiet established release, a retained reading after real sleep: none would earn the fifth stage alone. Together they would make later work possible. Peng fitted the sessions around actual archive duties. Tan watched the revised cup report waiting for the association's production proposal. The kiln carried two unfinished ambitions at once, one inside a person and one stacked carefully on a guarded shelf.

kiln_p06_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_031.text: On the first morning without Su Yan, Yue wanted the room to feel exactly as it had during her visit. It did not. The winter light entered from another angle, Han had left the brush bucket near the threshold, and Luo was busy resolving a delivery question before the session began. Yue moved the bucket and checked the cold references while waiting. The resulting ordinary order mattered more than preserving yesterday's mood. When Luo entered, he asked for the actual room condition. She could answer without saying that the important teacher was no longer there.

kiln_p06_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_032.text: They practised the existing release before any retained-reserve exercise. Yue knew the movement well enough to become careless about its end. Luo changed the command timing, and she discharged cleanly but let her shoulder rise afterward. The physical tension was not route failure. It could still grow into unnecessary strain if every small task ended that way. They repeated the ordinary relaxation without another admission. Yue found herself irritated by how much of cultivation consisted of not doing an extra thing. Luo grinned when she said so. The body preferred useful economy to dramatic loyalty.

kiln_p06_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_033.text: At the ordinary posture bench, they placed a light basket on a low table. Yue lifted it with a partner, then set it down without turning under load. Her right toe began to wander again at the last step. Luo asked her to reduce the distance and repeat on a later recovered occasion rather than force the foot inward while carrying. Today's observed limit was not an insult. It gave them a smaller movement that remained aligned. Yue wrote the task in ordinary words. She did not call a corrected walk an opened leg route.

kiln_p06_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_034.text: Jian watched from his approved cold schedule exercise and later asked why a fourth-stage person needed lessons in walking. Yue asked why an apprentice who could recite cooling intervals still needed a cold shelf. He said that was different, then failed to explain how. They both laughed. The comparison relieved Yue's embarrassment without diminishing the work. Jian offered to carry the basket from the other end when his task finished. She accepted the ordinary partner instead of using reinforcement to make the offer unnecessary. Their practice remained within the assigned load and ended before either needed to prove endurance.

kiln_p06_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_035.text: The week brought a small improvement in repeated alignment, followed by an ordinary bad morning after cold rain disturbed the lodging roof. Yue reported the sleep interruption before the room session. Luo changed it to chart review and ordinary unloaded movement. She resented the lost live practice until she noticed how often her attention wandered across the paper. The reduced session had not stolen a useful opportunity. It had prevented an exhausted version of herself from creating a result she could not honestly compare with the last recovered one.

kiln_p06_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_036.text: She spent the remaining assigned work period indexing the new candidate cup histories. Each successful guarded evaluation had a permitted load and reference, not a generic stamp reading good. The association instructor would receive the authorised copies with the actual vessels if the small set entered her room. Yue tied the records to the correct guarded storage positions and checked the count with Peng. The work suited a tired morning. It was still work. She had begun appreciating tasks that did not demand the same kind of attention from the body at every hour.

kiln_p06_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_037.text: Zhu invited her to trim ordinary practice feet after lunch, once the copying was complete. Yue made three useful rings and one foot too thin. They left the thin example in the practice rack and inspected why the tool angle changed at the end. Zhu said fatigue appeared in clay sooner than people liked to admit. Yue compared the foot with the morning's wandering attention. She could not diagnose every mood from a bowl, but the maker's ordinary condition belonged in a retained trial history. Today was practice, safely allowed to reveal what a final sample should not hide.

kiln_p06_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_038.text: Tan stopped beside the rack and asked whether ordinary production could ever be entirely free of tired makers. Zhu said no. It could be organised so that known fatigue did not carry tasks whose errors became hard to find later. A maker might prepare ordinary body on a day unsuitable for final joining. A schedule could allow handover instead of worshipping one person's endurance. Tan looked at the worker roster he carried. He had been counting available hours as if every hour had the same quality. Yue watched him make a small annotation rather than announce a conversion to wisdom.

kiln_p06_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_039.text: At the end of her next wage block, Yue sent a modest share home through the ordinary carrier. She retained enough for travel, personal necessities and the uncertain days after her placement. Peng showed her how to request the carrier's receipt without surrendering the only copy of her wage statement. The money did not purchase a new reserve. It bought family grain and reduced a worry that had followed Yue from earlier roads. She felt both poorer and lighter afterward. That complicated ordinary sensation seemed worth preserving in her private book beside the room's much simpler measurements.

kiln_p06_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_040.text: Her mother's next letter would take time, so Yue tried not to imagine its arrival every morning. Instead she helped Jian address his repaired toy cart to his brother. The ordinary carrier asked whether the parcel contained fragile ceramic. Jian proudly said no, then remembered that wood could also break. They packed it with clean scraps and allowed the permitted weight. Yue contributed a small written joke about the cart's desert rating. Jian removed the desert phrase before sealing, unwilling to confuse a young child for the sake of an adult's cleverness. She admired the correction.

kiln_p06_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_041.text: The association instructor came to collect the three tested cups for a limited supervised room use under the reviewed method. The transfer included inspection, permitted load, release conditions and return reporting for any fault. The larger production order remained unaccepted. Zhu watched the individual cups leave with mixed pleasure and unease. They had passed defined tests; she still cared what happened in real hands. Yue asked whether caring made her distrust the evidence. Zhu said it made her want the actual later history, rather than treating departure as the end of making.

kiln_p06_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_042.text: The instructor agreed to send ordinary usage reports after the first limited sessions. Nothing new was admitted merely because the cups arrived. The class room inspected them cold and used its own rated grounded bench and fuel. Yue accompanied the transfer only long enough to see the ordinary setup, then returned before her paid archive assignment. She did not become an instructor through curiosity or a fourth-stage title. The adults at the bench knew the method, and the learners had been told how to ask for a stop. Yue liked seeing the question about real hands find an actual room.

kiln_p06_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_043.text: Back at the kiln, Han asked whether their cups had bowed to the class before entering. Yue said they had behaved like cups and required someone else to carry them. He declared this an impressive limit for artifacts. Jian suggested that a cup able to walk would soon demand wages. Tan, passing with a fresh delivery note, said he would refuse to price its travel before seeing the actual legs. The joke drew all five of them into the same small absurdity. Yue noticed that Tan now laughed without first checking whether the owner stood nearby.

kiln_p06_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_044.text: Luo reviewed the week's actual work with her before the next supervised preparation session. The light partnered carry had become more consistent; the unloaded posture remained easier than the task under fatigue. The plan did not progress merely because a week had elapsed. They retained the last useful load and changed one ordinary condition at a time. Yue asked when she could expect a first new-route admission. Luo said after the reviewed prerequisites and Su Yan's next decision. An honest answer had become familiar enough that she could receive it without feeling the speaker had hidden a secret quicker path.

kiln_p06_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_045.text: They worked on recognising ordinary posterior calf tension separately from the chart's proposed fourth pair. Yue could feel a pull after standing on cold stone. It did not become evidence of an opened channel. Luo had her sit, move the ankle gently and describe what changed without any qi admission. The exercise felt almost embarrassingly simple. Then he placed the uncharged reference near her heel, and she discovered how readily expectation altered her account. She recorded the ambiguity. A future spiritual route needed to become distinguishable from ordinary signals, not to colonise every sensation in a leg.

kiln_p06_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_046.text: Zhu arrived after the session to find Yue glaring at her own heel. She asked what offense it had committed. Yue said it felt too much like a heel. Zhu considered that a promising sign. They walked to the bakery, where the repaired pipe held and the loaves smelled of ordinary heat. Yue tried explaining the chart exercise without making the heel seem mystical. Zhu listened, then said ordinary craft also required learning which scratch mattered and which simply looked dramatic under a lamp. They bought one loaf to share and took the longer dry path home.

kiln_p06_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_047.text: The next recovered reserve reading varied only slightly from the previous one. Yue had hoped for a larger increase because the week felt full of effort. Luo asked which part of that effort had actually addressed retention. She named the limited sessions, regular meals and sleep. The rest had supported her life and work, not necessarily expanded usable storage. They did not increase admission to reward disappointment. Yue left with a modest, comparable result and less desire to convert every difficult hour into a number. Some effort made a better day without making a larger reservoir.

kiln_p06_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_048.text: She told Peng this while helping bind the authorised cup-use report folder. The keeper said people sometimes wanted every useful task to receive the same kind of credit. Archive work, bodily practice and friendship left different traces. Refusing one universal total did not make the smaller traces worthless. Yue thought of Jian's apprenticeship claim and her letter home. The idea was obvious when spoken and difficult to inhabit. She sewed the next fold carefully, keeping the cover's opening on the correct side this time. Peng congratulated the cover on overcoming its first major philosophical obstacle.

kiln_p06_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_049.text: That afternoon the owner asked whether Yue would consider remaining after the nine-week archive placement. The larger teaching order might be declined, but ordinary work and the archive repairs still justified a smaller continued position. Any extension would specify paid hours and renew the finite practice arrangement separately. Yue did not accept immediately. She wanted to see the proposed terms, consult her own travel plans and understand whether training would remain supervised. The owner approved of the answer. A worker asking for real terms was easier to employ fairly than one offering unlimited gratitude.

kiln_p06_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_050.text: Yue discussed the possibility with Zhu on the cold loading step. Her friend looked pleased, then carefully avoided making the decision for her. Staying would bring ordinary companionship and months of useful practice. Leaving might offer other work and delay the new routes. Neither path was free of cost. Yue had spent earlier roads treating a place as valuable chiefly because it pointed to the next place. Here she could imagine value in another season of the same hall, if the terms remained sound. The thought felt like a change in ambition rather than its defeat.

kiln_p06_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_051.text: Jian wanted her to stay and said so without caution. He liked having someone near enough to laugh at him and distant enough from his family to hear complaints without repeating them upstream. Yue told him that was an expensive job description. He offered half a fried cake, then reconsidered because he had already eaten it. The ordinary joke left the real wish visible. She promised only to read the extension. He pretended this was disappointing and returned to his task. She watched him go, surprised by how quickly a new town could acquire people one feared leaving.

kiln_p06_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_052.text: Tan provided the draft extension at the owner's direction. Its ordinary archive hours did not depend on the unaccepted four hundred cups. The new practice allowance renewed by short reviewed blocks rather than promising endless machine fuel. Food and bed continued under the existing stated employment and authorised recovery terms. Yue checked the written scope against what the owner had said. Tan had copied it accurately. He asked whether she trusted the paper. She said she trusted it enough to ask him about one unclear renewal date. He corrected the date before requiring an answer.

kiln_p06_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_053.text: She wrote home about the possible stay, telling her mother the reason involved people and work as well as the fifth stage. The sentence surprised her when she read it back. She had not abandoned the desire for more pairs. She had found a place where the desire could grow beside other commitments without swallowing them. Her roommate asked whether that meant the Wandering Toe would become a permanent household resident. Yue said it remained under probation. The roommate offered it a warm sock, which was a joke and an actual useful gift.

kiln_p06_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_054.text: At the next ordinary meeting, the owner proposed giving apprentices the same advance notice of task changes that other paid workers received. A cold lesson could move if a live firing required the teacher, but the moved time and replacement task would be stated before the shift. Jian asked what happened if the notice came too late. Peng showed the claim path and the wage rule. The boy looked skeptical and less helpless. Yue's training plan had made a gap visible that affected more people than her. A useful personal ambition could change the room without making everyone a follower.

kiln_p06_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_055.text: Luo seemed tired after that meeting. He had spent years carrying informal teaching beside foreman duties, and now the informal work had become visible enough to need actual time. Yue asked whether the new plan burdened him. He said yes, and that pretending otherwise would make him a worse teacher. The owner would assign cold inspection tasks to another qualified worker so he could teach at the agreed times. His usefulness did not have to reside in doing everything. Yue recognised a lesson she preferred to receive through another person's admission than through another lecture at her own pride.

kiln_p06_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_056.text: The first limited cup-use report arrived from the association room. Under the documented modest method, all three vessels had released within their tested condition and remained sound under the specified cold checks. One learner found the handle awkward with a thick sleeve. That was an ordinary use issue worth studying, not proof of a charge failure. Zhu asked for the actual sleeve movement before altering future geometry. A change meant for comfort could narrow the rated clearance. Yue wrote the question and admired the way the maker refused to let a good report stop useful curiosity.

kiln_p06_057.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_057.text: The report also described a learner requesting a stop before admitting a trace. The instructor honoured the request and did not enter a failed demonstration. Yue read that detail twice. It was not her own training result, and the anonymous learner did not become a symbol required to make her wise. Still, she felt relief. The instruction written into a method had survived contact with a real impatient room. She placed the report in the public teaching extract after the authorised privacy check. Someone looking at the guarded failed cup could now see what a sound limited use looked like.

kiln_p06_058.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_058.text: Han objected that the success report lacked a joke. Peng said reports were permitted to be boring. He offered the title Three Cups Walk Into a Classroom and retired when nobody accepted it. Jian followed him to the broom rack and completed the joke loudly enough for the room to hear. Yue laughed while checking the report's three identities against the retained maker records. Humor and accuracy could share a room as long as nobody substituted one for the other. The cups had gone to class; the failed fourth had remained under a clear cover, still doing honest teaching work.

kiln_p06_059.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_059.text: At the week's last preparation session, Yue released both established arm tasks cleanly and kept the following ordinary movement relaxed. The small improvement pleased Luo because it reduced unnecessary tension rather than increasing input. Yue felt pleased too, without searching immediately for a larger reserve reading. She had become easier to supervise and less ready to hide disappointment. That change had no realm name. It would matter when the harder routes began. She left the room with the chart closed and went to help carry dry boards with a partner, taking the clear path around the bench.

kiln_p06_060.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_060.text: Before sleep, she copied the local fifth-stage method into her own study book, retaining its exact requirements and the reviewed date. She also kept the original signed plan where a future teacher could inspect it. The private margin held a simpler reminder: four pairs, one ordinary body. Her heel did not glow, her shoulder did not become invulnerable, and no new route opened because the words pleased her. She put the pencil down and listened to the household settle. A bed, a meal and a teacher's actual future appointment gave the next morning a shape she could inhabit.

kiln_p06_061.speaker: narrator
kiln_p06_061.text: The association's new proposal arrived at the end of the sixth week. It accepted the revised vessel geometry and brief demonstration method, then asked for four hundred cups within a winter interval too short for the work they had just measured. The price assumed the economical full-shelf schedule they had asked it to correct. Tan read the document twice, first as rescue for his accounts, then as a plan the hall must live inside. He took it to Luo before answering. Yue saw the route chart beneath her elbow and the impossible firing calendar above his. Both demanded real time.
